Project context

Juan Emilio Mier · Independent project, AI-assisted implementation

Created to explore the product design of developer evaluation tools. The design draws on the author's stated experience in AI evaluation; all examples here are original synthetic material, with no employer datasets or confidential workflows.

Design case study / Tracework v0.1

A score is a starting point.
Evidence is the interface.

A hypothesis-driven design exercise for an evaluation lead reviewing a candidate agent release.

Problem hypothesis

Aggregate evaluation scores can conceal different failure modes. Reviewers need a short path from a regression to the trace, rubric and decision. This is a product hypothesis, not a finding from completed user research.

Intended users

Primary: evaluation lead deciding whether a candidate is ready. Secondary: annotator documenting evidence; engineer investigating a failure. These are provisional roles, not interviewed participants.

Scope and constraints

Build an inspectable workflow without model credentials or proprietary data. Support comparison, prioritization, reasoned adjudication and export. Exclude live inference, team accounts, actual access control and production audit guarantees.

Success criteria to validate

Can a participant identify a tool-policy regression, explain their decision and export it without assistance? Measure completion, errors and time in a future usability study. No measured improvement is claimed.

Workflow 1 · Diagnose a regression

Scan the suiteSummary metrics show their denominator.
Open a caseRead the task and fixed rubric before the answer.
Compare tracesBaseline and candidate share a visual structure.
Inspect the failureReviewer notes explain where evaluation diverges.

Workflow 2 · Resolve disagreement

Filter the review queueUnresolved cases remain visible.
Choose a dispositionApprove, reject or request rerun.
Attach a reasonEmpty or whitespace-only notes cannot resolve a case.
Record and exportJSON carries fixture, timestamp, rubric version and rationale.

Decisions and tradeoffs

DecisionAlternative consideredReason / cost
Trace and rubric on the same screenSeparate analytics and annotation pagesPreserves context; requires denser content on small screens.
Explicit disagreement stateAverage reviewer scoresAverages can hide different interpretations; needs reviewer time.
Required rationaleOne-click approvalImproves inspectability at the cost of review speed.
Validated import + local storage + exportBackend and shared accountsMakes the prototype self-contained; cannot support trustworthy multi-user auditing.
Text + color status indicatorsColor-only signalsSupports different visual needs; browser accessibility testing remains pending.

Proposed usability session

Recruit 3–5 consenting evaluators. Ask them to locate the policy regression, resolve a disagreement, recover from a mistaken decision and export. Observe without coaching; record task success, hesitation and interpretation errors. Ask permission before recording.

Next iteration should be driven by observed failures, not a claim that this version has been validated.

Engineering handoff

Entities: suite, test, model run, rubric, review, decision event. Production needs authenticated reviewers, server-enforced permissions, durable versioned fixtures, append-only events, idempotent writes and export authorization.

Implementation / validation / provenance

Built to be inspected.

Runnable source, explicit rule semantics and an honest boundary between a useful prototype and a production evaluation platform.

What actually runs

Eight synthetic cases exercise authorization boundaries, grounding, ambiguous recipients, untrusted instructions, tool failures and supplied performance budgets. Six rule types evaluate outputs and event names deterministically. Human decisions are recorded separately.

Download source, tests and documentation ↓

Verification performed

17 engine tests cover pass/fail behavior, regression totals, exact event matching, inclusive budgets, review history, changed-case invalidation, import/export round trips, duplicate IDs and invalid input. Syntax and HTML target checks passed.

Native Figma desktop and mobile designs were visually inspected. Browser rendering and end-to-end UI testing remain pending because the browser connection was unavailable.

Design artifacts

Editable documentation, desktop and mobile review layouts, reusable case and metric components, bound color variables and text styles. These are native design explorations, not screenshots of the application.

Open editable design ↗

Data and limitations

No model API is called. Text rules use case-insensitive substring matching; event rules use exact names. Cost and latency are supplied fixture values. Local storage is device-specific and editable. No authenticated reviewers, tamper-proof history or customer adoption are claimed.

AI collaboration and authorship

This independent project was initiated for Juan Emilio Mier. ChatGPT/Codex generated implementation and draft documentation. It uses original synthetic examples, with no confidential employer data. No use of Claude Code or completed user research is claimed. Usability sessions and stakeholder review remain planned work. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
